title: Muppet: Massive Multi-task Representations with Pre-Finetuning
abstract: We propose pre-finetuning, an additional largescale learning stage between language model pre-training and fine-tuning. Pre-finetuning is massively multi-task learning (around 50 datasets, over 4.8 million total labeled examples), and is designed to encourage learning of representations that generalize better to many different tasks. We show that prefinetuning consistently improves performance for pretrained discriminators (e.g. RoBERTa) and generation models (e.g. BART) on a wide range of tasks (sentence prediction, commonsense reasoning, MRC, etc.), while also significantly improving sample efficiency during fine-tuning. We also show that large-scale multi-tasking is crucial; pre-finetuning can hurt performance when few tasks are used up until a critical point (usually above 15) after which performance improves linearly in the number of tasks.

claims.text: Pre-finetuning across massively multi-task supervised datasets consistently improves downstream performance for both pretrained discriminators (e.g., RoBERTa) and generation models (e.g., BART).
Pre-finetuned language models significantly improve sample efficiency during task-specific fine-tuning, requiring less data to achieve high accuracy.

Multi-task pre-finetuning exhibits a critical point in task scale (usually above 15 tasks), below which performance degrades compared to standard pre-training and above which performance improves linearly with the number of tasks.
Using task-heterogeneous batches combined with inverse-log uniform loss scaling significantly improves multi-task training stability and downstream evaluation performance.
RoBERTa-Large with pre-finetuning achieves an accuracy of 92.8 on RTE.
RoBERTa-Large with pre-finetuning achieves an accuracy of 86.4 on HellaSwag.

limitations.text: Standard multi-task learning schemes over pre-trained models can be unstable and fail to learn high-quality representations when operating with diverse datasets.
Pre-finetuning with fewer than approximately 15 tasks degrades model representations and leads to worse downstream fine-tuning performance than standard pre-trained baselines.
Using a separate task head for each individual Commonsense and MRC dataset led to severe overfitting during pre-finetuning.
